title: Officer found bruised, bloody, inquest hears
article: A Sicamous RCMP constable was beaten before killing his assailant with a gunshot to the neck, a coroner's inquest was told Wednesday.
RCMP Sgt. Jim Harrison testified that when he arrived on the scene of the shooting, Const. Rob Romaniuk was bruised, bloody and in a state of shock.
An autopsy showed Graham John Maryancik, 29, died May 26, 2004, from severe bleeding and trauma caused by the gunshot wound, said Dr. James Stephen, a forensic pathologist.

Stephen revealed details of the autopsy to Jeff Dolan, a B.C. regional coroner, Helen Roberts, lawyer for the RCMP, Sydney Pilley, lawyer for the coroner, and a five-member jury on the first day of a scheduled three-day inquest.

"The cause of death was a gunshot wound to the left side of his neck. ... The muzzle (of the gun) was held close to the skin. This could be determined by gunpowder being found around the entry wound," he said.
A bullet also grazed Maryancik's right bicep, but the wound wasn't significant, he said.
Romaniuk, who fired the shots, was called to a motor vehicle accident at the Last Spike rest stop at about 11:45 p.m. that night.
A Ford Windstar minivan had pulled into the rest stop at Craigellachie, bounced off the rear of a semi-trailer, struck a parked car and then rolled down an embankment.
Harrison said he arrived about 45 minutes after the shooting and took Romaniuk's statement.
"I noticed blood on Romaniuk's face and arms. His soft-body armour was ripped off at the shoulder and shirt was ripped," he said.
Reading from Romaniuk's statement, Harrison said: "I pulled up and saw a van in the water.
"There was thumping coming from the van and I called out to the driver," he read.
The driver, Maryancik, got out of the minivan and crawled up the embankment. The two men talked briefly before Romaniuk said in his statement that he asked see to Maryancik's driver's licence.
Maryancik went back to his vehicle, where he stayed long enough for Romaniuk to grow worried. The officer was walking back to his police car when Maryancik attacked him.
"Maryancik grabbed him by his soft-body armour and hit him in the face several times," Harrison told the jury. "Romaniuk hit him in the face twice with his flashlight but that didn't phase him."
Maryancik, who was six feet tall and 242 pounds, threw Romaniuk to the concrete and held him down, Harrison said.
He continued punching the constable before Romaniuk drew his gun and fired twice.

Members of the Eagle Valley rescue squad and B.C. Ambulance service told the jury Maryancik was face down on the concrete when they arrived at 12:10 a.m. The man had no pulse when he was loaded into an ambulance and taken to Shuswap Lake General Hospital. Doctors pronounced him dead shortly after 1 a.m.
Stephen said toxicology results showed Maryancik had trace amounts of marijuana and OxyContin, a sedative prescribed to treat moderate or severe pain, in his bloodstream.
"These wouldn't have contributed to his death," he said.
Harrison said Maryancik was known to RCMP in Revelstoke, where he had a history of violent behaviour and was rumoured to associate with Hells Angels.
"They had a notice out to all officers that he should not be approached without two members present," he said.
